flags.what: Runs eligible ops in a lower precision dtype inside the context; the dtype defaults per device.
flags.default: torch.float16 on cuda, torch.bfloat16 on cpu
flags.scope: CUDA, ROCm, CPU, XPU, HPU, MTIA, MAIA

flags.what: Scales the loss so small FP16 gradients do not underflow; replaces the deprecated torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler (likewise torch.cuda.amp.autocast is deprecated).
Lets FP32 matmuls use TF32 or a bfloat16x3 split ("high") or bfloat16 ("medium"); "highest" keeps full FP32.
Newer (after 2.9) switch for FP32 matmuls: "ieee", "tf32", or "bfx9" (BF16x9 emulation, CUDA 12.9+ build).
flags.scope: CUDA (bfx9 emulation only on compute capability 10.0 / 10.3)

flags.what: Newer switch for FP32 cuDNN convolutions; siblings are torch.backends.cudnn.rnn.fp32_precision and torch.backends.cudnn.fp32_precision.
Global setting that the backend-specific fp32_precision settings follow unless they are set explicitly.
Older switch allowing TF32 in FP32 matmuls; the docs say it is going to be deprecated in favour of fp32_precision.
Older switch allowing TF32 in cuDNN convolutions; going to be deprecated in favour of fp32_precision.
Set False to force full precision (not FP16) intermediate reductions inside FP16 GEMMs.
Set False to force full precision intermediate reductions inside BF16 GEMMs.
Lets FP16 GEMMs accumulate entirely in FP16 for speed, at a cost in precision and overflow risk.
Lets FP32 matmuls on the oneDNN (mkldnn) backend compute internally in bf16 or tf32; conv and rnn have matching settings.
Mixed precision on Intel GPUs; use torch.amp.GradScaler(device="xpu") for FP16 training (needs FP64 hardware support).
Lets matmul-type operators use the HF32 format, like torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32.
flags.scope: Huawei Ascend NPU (Atlas training and inference series)

flags.what: Lets convolution operators use the HF32 format, like torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32.
flags.scope: Huawei Ascend NPU (Atlas training and inference series)

flags.what: Old switches that cast float tensors to bf16 on XLA devices; warn from Torch-XLA 2.5, to be removed (Torch-XLA 2.8). Use torch.autocast(dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_type='xla') or model.to(torch.bfloat16).
Turns TF32 off so FP32 matmuls and convolutions run at full FP32; on TPU it also stops bfloat16 use for FP32 ops.
Sets the global dtype policy: "mixed_float16" or "mixed_bfloat16" compute in 16 bits with float32 variables.
Keras 2 name; in current TensorFlow docs it is an alias of tf.keras.config.set_dtype_policy (Keras 3).
Default precision of matmuls and convolutions on 32-bit inputs: e.g. "bfloat16", "tensorfloat32", "float32", or an algorithm preset like "BF16_BF16_F32_X3". Env var JAX_DEFAULT_MATMUL_PRECISION.
Per-call precision: DEFAULT (bf16 on TPU, TF32 on GPU if available), HIGH (3 bf16 passes on TPU), HIGHEST (6 bf16 passes on TPU, FP32 on GPU).
dtype sets the computation dtype and param_dtype the stored parameter dtype; precision passes a jax.lax.Precision.
Overrides defaults and code settings so cuBLAS does not use TF32 Tensor Cores for single precision.

Math mode per handle: CUBLAS_DEFAULT_MATH, CUBLAS_PEDANTIC_MATH, CUBLAS_TF32_TENSOR_OP_MATH, CUBLAS_FP32_EMULATED_BF16X9_MATH, CUBLAS_FP64_EMULATED_FIXEDPOINT_MATH; OR in CUBLAS_MATH_DISALLOW_REDUCED_PRECISION_REDUCTION. CUBLAS_TENSOR_OP_MATH is deprecated.
Compute type for cublasGemmEx / cuBLASLt; FP32 alternatives are CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_FAST_16F, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_FAST_16BF, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_EMULATED_16BFX9.
Runs TE layers in FP8/FP4 under a recipe (DelayedScaling, Float8CurrentScaling, Float8BlockScaling, MXFP8BlockScaling, NVFP4BlockScaling). Replaces te.fp8_autocast(fp8_recipe=...), deprecated in 2.9.
flags.scope: NVIDIA GPUs with FP8 Tensor Cores

flags.what: Overrides the compute type of GEMMs that request XF32: -1 off, 0 F32, 1 XF32, 2 F32_BF16.
Lets CUDA libraries used by CuPy compute 32-bit float operations with TF32 Tensor Cores.

Default fpmath mode allowing implicit f32 down-conversion: strict, bf16, f16, tf32 (accelerated on Intel GPUs only) or any. C API: dnnl_set_default_fpmath_mode; per primitive dnnl::primitive_attr::set_fpmath_mode.
flags.scope: Intel CPU/GPU, Arm (via Arm Compute Library)

flags.what: No global matmul precision switch on the data types page; precision is chosen by array dtype (float16, bfloat16, float32; float64 CPU only).

notes: PyTorch stable docs redirect to 2.15 (Nov 2026); all PyTorch URLs are pinned to 2.15.

PyTorch docs give no explicit default for the new fp32_precision settings (CUDA) or for allow_fp16_reduced_precision_reduction; the FP16 text implies reduced precision reductions are allowed by default, but this is not stated.

torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision bfx9: backends.html says BF16x9 emulation only applies on compute capability 10.0 or 10.3; other architectures use native FP32. Using bfx9 for the generic, cuDNN or mkldnn settings raises an error.

torch.backends.mkldnn.matmul.fp32_precision: the 2.15 mkldnn notes show values ieee, bf16 and tf32 but do not list the full set or name the hardware beyond a benchmark on SPR (Sapphire Rapids). backends.html does not document mkldnn fp32_precision.
torch.backends.cuda.preferred_blas_library ("cublas", "cublaslt", "ck" on ROCm; env TORCH_BLAS_PREFER_CUBLASLT=1) is experimental and picks the library, not the precision; left out.

MPS: PyTorch 2.15 MPS notes state MPS does not support torch.float64 or torch.complex128; the amp page lists no MPS autocast default and backends.html has no MPS precision setting. MPS autocast support not confirmed on a fetched page.
XPU autocast default dtype not stated on the fetched page (examples pass float16 explicitly). GradScaler on XPU requires FP64 hardware; disable it on Arc A-Series.

torch_xla: no current pytorch/xla page found stating XLA_USE_BF16 status (docs.pytorch.org/xla dtype pages returned 404). Row sourced from AWS Neuron official migration guide; a pytorch/xla PR #7582 'remove XLA_USE_BF16 and other variants' was merged (not fetched).

torch_npu: also torch_npu.npu.aclnn.allow_hf32 exists per search results (not fetched). Ascend docs pages on hiascend.com are JS-rendered; rows come from Ascend's op-plugin 7.3.0 docs on gitcode (Chinese).

Keras 3 policy page mentions keras.mixed_precision.set_dtype_policy in a docstring; TF API page lists tf.keras.mixed_precision.set_dtype_policy and set_global_policy as aliases of tf.keras.config.set_dtype_policy (Keras 3.15.1 source). Default global policy float32 is from the policy page reset example, not a stated default.
cuBLAS: CUBLAS_EMULATION_STRATEGY env var (performant or eager) overrides the emulation strategy for BF16x9 / fixed-point emulation; not given its own row.

Transformer Engine: current API page (2.18) lists fp8_autocast and fp8_model_init under 'Deprecated functions' and recipe classes DelayedScaling, MXFP8BlockScaling, NVFP4BlockScaling, Float8CurrentScaling, Float8BlockScaling, CustomRecipe; the exact autocast signature (enabled=True, calibrating=False, recipe=None, amax_reduction_group=None) came from a search snippet of the 2.16 API page, not a full fetch. Per-recipe GPU requirements not confirmed. fp8_model_init is deprecated in favour of quantized_model_init.
ROCm: hipBLASLt documents HIPBLASLT_OVERRIDE_COMPUTE_TYPE_XF32 only; rocBLAS env vars not checked. HIPBLASLT_ALLOW_TF32 (seen in PyTorch ROCm code) is not on the hipBLASLt env var page.
JAX: jax.default_matmul_precision context manager not confirmed on a fetched page. Ascend ENABLE_HF32_EXECUTION env var is for TensorFlow 1.15 on CANN (search result only).
MLX: data types page has no mixed precision or matmul precision setting; float64 arrays on the GPU raise an exception.
